pages.title: Tailscale: connecting to our game
pages.description: How to get ready, what Tailscale is and why we use it, what is safe and what happens on game day, with two short recordings and their transcripts.

grids.title: Get ready
grids.note: Do steps 1 and 2 before game day. Steps 3 and 4 happen when your link arrives.
rows: Go to tailscale.com/download/windows. Click the Windows download. Open the file. Windows asks for permission once. Check the publisher says Tailscale Inc., then click Yes. Tick the license box. Click Install, then Close. Every click is spelled out in the audio below.

Right-click the Tailscale icon by the clock. Click Log in. Pick Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub. Use a personal account, not a work or school one. If it asks, choose Personal use. Remember which account you used.
The host sends you your personal join link privately on game day. It is never on this site, and nobody posts it in public.

Open your link in your browser. If asked, sign in with the same account as step 2. Click the button that accepts. Right-click the Tailscale icon and open Network devices. You should see the host’s PC listed.

grids.title: What Tailscale is, and why we use it
grids.note: Tailscale is an app. It is how your PC reaches the host’s game PC.
rows: An app that makes a private, encrypted link between devices. It uses an open source standard called WireGuard.
It lets you reach the host’s game PC without opening anything on anyone’s router. Only people the host shares with can connect.
A Windows 10 or 11 PC with internet. A personal Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub sign-in, which is free. You run no scripts and change no router settings.

grids.title: Is this safe?
grids.note: Each statement below matches Tailscale’s own documentation.
rows: Only the host’s game PC, and only the game port. The host set that rule in Tailscale. You cannot reach anything else of the host’s.
Can the host reach my PC?

No. A shared PC can answer your PC. It cannot start a connection to your devices. Tailscale says you can accept a share with no risk of exposing your own network. That changes only if you share a machine back.
What does the host’s side learn?
Your account’s email address and picture. Also the real network address of your Tailscale device. The connection needs both.
Tailscale does not expose it. The exception is an advanced feature called a subnet router, which you would have to set up yourself.
What about my normal internet use?
It does not go through Tailscale or through the host. Tailscale only carries traffic between devices that run it, unless you choose an exit node yourself.
How do I turn it off?

Right-click the Tailscale icon by the clock and choose to disconnect. To remove it, open Settings, then Apps, find Tailscale, and press Uninstall. That does not delete the device from your account, so also remove it on the Machines page of the Tailscale admin console. The host can end the share at any time.
Your join link. Treat it like a password.

grids.title: What happens on game day
rows: Make sure its icon is by the clock. It stops when you sign out or restart. If so, open it from the Start menu.
Double-click your SkyrimTogether.exe shortcut. Finish the Helgen start offline first. Then load your campaign character.
Press F2 or Right Ctrl. Click Connect. Type the address and password the host sends you privately. Click Connect again.
You hear a confirmation. The small chat window says “Successfully connected to server.”

Check Tailscale is running and the host’s PC shows in Network devices. Signed in with a different account than the one that accepted the share? Right-click the icon and switch accounts. Still stuck? Send the host the exact message. Hide the address and password in any screenshot.

clips.title: Tailscale: is this safe?
clips.summary: What Tailscale is, what the host can and cannot see, and how to turn it off.
transcript: Is this safe?
What Tailscale is. Tailscale is an app that makes a private, encrypted connection between devices. It uses an open source standard called WireGuard.
What you are joining. The host shares one PC with you. Once you accept, your PC can reach that one PC and nothing else of the host's.

It only goes one way. A shared PC can answer your PC, but it cannot start connections to your devices. Tailscale says you can accept a share with no risk of exposing your own network. That only changes if you share a machine back.
What the host's side does learn. Your account's email address and picture, and the real network address of your Tailscale device, because the connection needs them.
Your home network. Tailscale does not expose it unless you deliberately set up an advanced feature called a subnet router.
Your normal internet traffic. It does not go through Tailscale or through the host. Tailscale only carries traffic between devices that run it, unless you choose an exit node yourself.

Turning it off. Right-click the Tailscale icon by the clock and choose to disconnect. To remove it, open Settings, then Apps, find Tailscale, and press Uninstall. Uninstalling does not delete the device from your account, so also remove it on the Machines page of the Tailscale admin console. The host can end the share at any time.
Keep the invite link private. Treat it like a password.

clips.title: Tailscale: setup, step by step
clips.summary: Every click and prompt: install, sign in, accept the share, connect in the game, and the usual fixes.
transcript: Join the host's Skyrim Together server with Tailscale. This works on Windows 10 and Windows 11.

You need a Windows PC with internet, a personal Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub account, which is free, the host's share link, and the address and password the host sends you privately. Nothing here asks you to run scripts, open ports, change router settings, or give admin rights beyond the one Windows prompt in Part 1.
Part 1. Install Tailscale on your PC.
Step 1. Open tailscale dot com, slash download, slash windows, and click the Windows download button. You get a file whose name starts with tailscale setup, in your Downloads folder.

Step 2. Double-click it. Windows asks, Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device? Check that the verified publisher says Tailscale Inc., then click Yes. This is the only permission prompt. A standard account is asked for an admin password. A window called Tailscale Setup opens.

Step 3. Tick the box that says, I agree to the license terms and conditions. Leave Options alone, and click Install. It downloads about 38 megabytes, so stay online. When it says Installation Successfully Completed, click Close. A Tailscale icon appears next to the clock. Click the up arrow if you cannot see it.
Step 4. Right-click the Tailscale icon and click Log in. The very first time, a welcome window may appear first. If so, use its sign-in button. Your browser opens a Tailscale sign-in page.

Step 5. Choose Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub, and sign in with a personal account, not a work or school one. There is no separate email sign-up. If it asks Business use or Personal use, pick Personal use. If it asks you to add a second device, click Take me home, or close the tab. Right-clicking the icon now shows your account. Remember it. Part 2 needs the same one.
Windows 10 or 11. It is the same installer and the same steps. The Windows 11 prompts look a little different, but say the same words.
Part 2. Accept the host's share link.
Step 1. Paste the share link the host sent you into your browser and press Enter.
Step 2. If Tailscale asks you to sign in, use the same account as in Part 1. You should see the host's invitation to a shared PC.
Step 3. Click the button that accepts the invitation. The shared PC is now available to your account, and only to you.
Step 4. Right-click the Tailscale icon and open Network devices. You should see the host's PC listed. It cannot start connections back to you. You connect to it.
An unused link stops working after 30 days. If the page says the invitation is no longer valid, ask the host for a new link.
Part 3. Connect in Skyrim Together.
Step 1. Finish the Helgen introduction first. Start the game from your Skyrim Together shortcut, and make sure Tailscale is running. Its icon is next to the clock.
Step 2. Press Right Control, or F two, then click Connect. You should see an Address box and a Password box.

Step 3. In the Address box, type the address the host sent you privately, then a colon, then one zero five seven eight. The address starts with the numbers one hundred dot, or is a name ending in dot t s dot net.
Step 4. In the Password box, type the password the host sent you privately, then click Connect. You should hear a confirmation, and see Successfully connected to server, in the small chat window.
Step 5. If you see, Could not connect to the specified server, use the fixes below and try again. If it says the server has a different version of Skyrim Together, tell the host.
If something goes wrong.

If you signed in with a different account than the one that accepted the share, right-click the Tailscale icon, click the account shown at the top, and choose the account that accepted the share. If it is not listed, choose Add another account, and sign in with it. Then check Network devices again.

If Tailscale is not running, sign in to Windows and open Tailscale from the Start menu. Wait until the icon's menu shows your account. It stops when you sign out or restart. A Windows note saying No internet access on the Tailscale network is harmless.

If the share was not accepted, and the host's PC is not in Network devices, open the share link again and accept it with the same account. If it is no longer valid, ask the host for a new one. Use a personal account, because a work or school account may be refused.
See a window this sheet does not describe? Stop, and send the host a screenshot with the address and password hidden.

after.title: Leaving and coming back later
items: Your progress lives in your own save, on your own PC. The server keeps no save of your character or the world.
Save before you leave. Then disconnect and quit to the main menu:
has the steps.
To come back, load your latest campaign save and connect the usual way. Check the usual leader and regroup before questing. Rejoining with a full group is not tested yet.
The server is its own program on the host's PC, so it can run while the host is not in the game. Nobody has tested friends playing without the host in the game yet.

Playing your campaign character alone, offline, moves your save on. Quests you advance alone may not match the group's. Our rule: do not advance the main campaign without missing players, and do not quest alone to catch up (
). For solo time, use a separate character, as a smaller-party night does.

grids.title: Leaving
rows: Save if possible (Esc → Save). Let it finish. Press F2, choose Disconnect, then Proceed. Choose Quit to Main Menu (Esc → System → Quit), which works properly under Skyrim Together. If you have a moment, step somewhere safe first. Exiting the program itself crashes at the very end on our Skyrim Together versions. Your save is already written, so it is harmless apart from a crash file. No fix is proven.
Short break: type BRB. Done tonight: say so. Tell the group later if needed. No recap needed.
Short break: pause quests until everyone returns. Done tonight: save and stop this campaign. Resume together next session.

columns: What it does in our game
